Operator: Good day, and welcome to the SecureNet Technologies Second Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss SecureNet Technologies' results for the second quarter of fiscal 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Technology Officer; Morgan Patel, Chief Security Officer; and Casey Wong, VP of Sales.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. SecureNet Technologies continues to demonstrate leadership in the cybersecurity market. We achieved record bookings in the second quarter, driven by strong demand for our integrated security platform and our expanding global presence. The positive customer feedback about Nexus AI Sentinel and the resulting surge in adoption across our enterprise base is very encouraging.

We are focused on six strategic priorities: enhancing marketing spend efficiency to drive scalable growth, leveraging customer feedback on new products and features to accelerate innovation, sustaining strong ARR growth rates both quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year, expanding the number of customers with ARR over $100K, delivering billings performance that exceeds guidance, and maintaining robust R&D investment as a percentage of revenue to stay ahead of evolving threats.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. We delivered another quarter of strong financial results. Total revenue for the second quarter was $285 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. We saw significant growth in our subscription revenue, which now accounts for 92% of our total revenue. Gross margin was 78%, while operating expenses were $195 million. Net income was $52 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.72. We are reiterating our full-year guidance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial objectives.

As we dive deeper into our financials, I'd like to spend some time on several key areas that highlight our execution in this hyper-competitive cybersecurity landscape. With ransomware attacks up 37% year-over-year per Chainalysis data and nation-state threats escalating—think the recent Change Healthcare breach—demand for our next-gen endpoint detection and response (EDR), secure access service edge (SASE), and zero-trust platform remains robust. But we're not just riding the wave; we're optimizing every dollar to acquire high-value enterprise customers with lifetime values often exceeding $5 million.

First, on marketing spend efficiency, a critical lever for driving sustainable growth. In Q2, we deployed $28.2 million in marketing spend, a 12% increase year-over-year but flat sequentially as we lap last year's heavy event investments post-RSA Conference ramp-up. This represents just 14% of our total revenue—down from 18% in Q2 2023—reflecting maturing scale efficiencies akin to what we've seen at peers like CrowdStrike and Zscaler. The result? Customer acquisition cost (CAC) dropped 22% to $142,000 per enterprise deal, our lowest ever, driven by a 28% improvement in marketing-qualified lead (MQL) to sales-qualified lead (SQL) conversion, now at 41%. Payoff? Marketing-attributed annual contract value (ACV) hit $312 million, delivering a stellar 4.8x return on marketing investment (ROMI), up from 3.2x last year.

Breaking it down by channel, account-based marketing (ABM) continues to be our North Star, accounting for 52% of spend at $14.7 million. We're laser-focused on the Fortune 2000, using 6sense and Demandbase for intent data to target accounts showing signals like 'ransomware preparedness' or 'cloud migration' spikes. This yielded a 15x ROAS on ABM campaigns, with win rates 3x higher than broad digital efforts. Digital channels—28% of spend, or $7.9 million—leaned heavily into LinkedIn and Google Ads, optimized with our proprietary AI lead-scoring engine built on Snowflake data warehouse. Here, cost per MQL fell 31% to $450, thanks to hyper-personalized ads referencing real-time threats from MITRE ATT&CK frameworks. Content syndication via Dark Reading and SC Media drove 62,000 gated downloads of our 'Zero-Trust in Hybrid Environments' whitepaper series, converting at 18%—a benchmark that rivals Palo Alto's Prisma campaigns.

Events and partnerships made up the balance at 20%, or $5.6 million. We trimmed physical events by 40% from 2023 levels amid cost discipline, pivoting to virtual roadshows co-hosted with MSSPs like Accenture and Deloitte. Our booth at Black Hat USA generated 1,200 SQLs at a CAC payback of under 6 months, bolstered by live demos of our XDR platform's behavioral AI, which caught 94% of novel malware in our latest AV-TEST Labs certification.

Regionally, North America remains our efficiency powerhouse at 68% of spend, with CAC at $118,000 and 5.2x ROMI, fueled by regulatory tailwinds like SEC cyber disclosure rules pushing CISOs to act. EMEA, at 22% of spend, saw a 19% CAC reduction to $165,000, driven by GDPR enforcement and NIS2 directives; our localized campaigns around DORA compliance resonated strongly in financial services verticals. APAC, now 10% of spend at $2.8 million, is our growth accelerator—up 45% YoY—with CAC at $192,000 but trending down 14% QoQ. Initiatives like partnering with NTT for Japan market entry and tailoring content for PDPA in Singapore are paying off, with SQL velocity up 25% amid rising state-sponsored attacks from the Lazarus Group.

Strategically, we're embedding gen-AI across the funnel to sustain these gains. Our 'Marketing Intelligence Platform'—powered by integrations with Salesforce Einstein and our own threat telemetry from 15 billion daily events—automates 70% of campaign optimization, predicting MQL quality with 87% accuracy. This mirrors industry shifts, as Gartner notes 65% of cyber vendors will adopt AI-driven ABM by 2025. We're also doubling down on customer advocacy: Net Promoter Score hit 68, enabling 35% of new logos via peer references, slashing CAC by 40% on those deals.

Before moving on, I'd like to touch on one of our brightest spots this quarter: customer feedback on our new products and features. As many of you know, we've been aggressively innovating in our platform to address the evolving threat landscape—think state-sponsored APTs, ransomware-as-a-service proliferation like LockBit 3.0, and the persistent fallout from supply chain vulnerabilities à la SolarWinds and Log4j. Our customers aren't just buying cybersecurity; they're demanding proactive, AI-native solutions that scale with their hybrid cloud environments.

We've been tracking this rigorously via our Voice of the Customer program, powered by Medallia and integrated directly into our Nexus One unified platform. Our Net Promoter Score (NPS) for new feature adoption surged 22 points quarter-over-quarter to 68—that's leadership territory in the G2 Grid for Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), where we're now a Leader alongside CrowdStrike and Microsoft Defender. Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) hit 92% for our beta cohorts, with 87% of respondents citing 'immediate ROI' from reduced mean time to detect (MTTD) and respond (MTTR). Churn among new product users dropped 15% YoY to under 2%, and we've seen a 28% uplift in net expansion revenue from upsells—think expanding from EDR to our full Extended Detection and Response (XDR) stack.

Diving into specifics, our flagship launch—Nexus AI Sentinel, our GenAI-powered threat hunting module—has been a game-changer. Launched in Q1, it's already live with 4,200 customers, representing 35% penetration of our top-tier enterprise base. Feedback highlights a 65% reduction in false positives compared to legacy SIEM tools like Splunk or Elastic, thanks to our proprietary multimodal LLMs trained on 15 petabytes of anonymized telemetry data. One Fortune 500 financial services client in EMEA reported slashing alert fatigue by 72%, freeing their SOC team to focus on high-fidelity incidents. Quantitatively, early adopters are seeing 40% faster threat remediation, with MTTR averaging 17 minutes versus the industry benchmark of 45 from Ponemon's latest Cost of a Data Breach report.

On the Zero Trust front, our Nexus Edge Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) 2.0 feature, with integrated Secure Web Gateway (SWG) and Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) capabilities, garnered 91% positive feedback in usability surveys. We've embedded SASE principles here, drawing inspiration from Zscaler's model but with native post-quantum cryptography readiness—critical as NIST's PQC standards roll out next year. Adoption spiked 52% in Q2, driven by compliance needs around GDPR and the EU's NIS2 Directive. Regional breakdown: North America accounts for 55% of deployments, with a NPS of 72; APAC jumped to 28% share, up 40% QoQ, fueled by Singapore's PDPA enhancements and Australia's Essential Eight maturity model—clients like a major telco in Sydney praised the frictionless SaaS-to-on-prem hybrid support.

We also rolled out Nexus CloudShield, our Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) and Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) suite, which integrates seamlessly with AWS GuardDuty, Azure Sentinel, and Google Chronicle. Feedback from 1,800 early users shows 84% reporting 50%+ improvements in misconfiguration detection, aligning with Gartner’s 2024 CSPM Magic Quadrant where we're challenging for Visionary status. A key trend here: 62% of feedback mentions 'genuine shift-left security' for DevSecOps pipelines, with integrations to GitHub Actions and Jenkins yielding 3x faster remediation in CI/CD workflows.

Of course, no launch is without learnings. About 12% of feedback flagged initial onboarding friction for smaller MSPs—we've addressed this with a new self-service Nexus Academy portal, which has already boosted CSAT by 18 points in pilot groups. Geopolitically, we're monitoring U.S.-China tensions impacting supply chain trust; our U.S.-based data sovereignty features resonated strongly with 95% of federal-adjacent customers pursuing CMMC 2.0 Level 2 certification.

Strategically, this feedback validates our 'platformization' bet: 76% of customers are now multi-product, up from 52% last year, as we consolidate point solutions from vendors like SentinelOne and Palo Alto Prisma. We're doubling down with Q3 betas for Nexus Quantum-Resilient VPN and autonomous SOAR playbooks, targeting a 25% NPS lift. Partnerships with hyperscalers—AWS Marketplace revenue up 60%, Microsoft co-sell deals converting at 45%—are accelerating this flywheel. In summary, customer love for our innovations is fueling 32% YoY ARR growth to $1.42 billion, with new product ACV at a record $187K. We're not just keeping pace with the 14.5% CAGR cybersecurity market per IDC; we're outrunning it.

Shifting to ARR growth, which continues to underscore the strength of our platform. For Q2 FY2024, our total ARR reached $1.28 billion, up an impressive 12% quarter-over-quarter from $1.14 billion in Q1. This QoQ acceleration—our strongest in three quarters—reflects robust new logo wins and expansions amid escalating global threats, including the recent surge in AI-orchestrated ransomware campaigns like those mimicking LockBit 4.0 variants.

On a year-over-year basis, ARR grew 32% to $1.28 billion from $968 million in Q2 FY2023. This marks our 11th straight quarter of 30%+ YoY growth, outpacing the overall cybersecurity market's estimated 15-18% expansion per Gartner’s latest forecasts. For context, our dollar-based net retention rate—or NRR—held steady at 118%, driven by 85% of customers expanding their seat counts or adding modules like our Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) overlay, which saw 45% YoY adoption growth.

Breaking it down by segment, our Enterprise ARR—representing 72% of total ARR—surged 35% YoY to $920 million, fueled by multi-year deals with Fortune 500 names in financial services and healthcare. Mid-market ARR, at 28% of the mix, grew 25% YoY to $360 million, benefiting from our streamlined Sentinel XDR trials converting at a 65% attach rate. Notably, our consumption-based pricing for AI threat hunting added $45 million in incremental ARR this quarter alone, as customers scale usage amid the 40% rise in generative AI exploits reported by MITRE ATT&CK.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse, contributing 62% of ARR with 34% YoY growth, anchored by hyperscaler partnerships like our deepened integration with AWS Graviton processors for edge security. EMEA accelerated to 28% YoY growth—our fastest in the region—thanks to NIS2 Directive compliance deadlines, where we displaced legacy vendors like Check Point in key wins at European banks. APAC, now 10% of ARR, delivered 42% YoY growth, propelled by data sovereignty mandates in Japan and Australia; we closed a landmark $50 million ARR deal with a major telco there, bundling our Quantum SASE with 5G slicing protections.

Strategically, this ARR momentum ties directly to three initiatives. First, our GenAI Shield launch, which uses proprietary large language models to preempt polymorphic malware—already driving 20% of new ARR from early adopters competing with CrowdStrike’s Charlotte AI. Second, platform consolidation: 60% of expansions came from customers migrating from point solutions like Symantec Endpoint or McAfee MVISION, with our average contract value up 22% YoY to $1.2 million. Third, we’re leaning into OT/IoT security, where ARR grew 55% YoY to $120 million, addressing critical infrastructure vulnerabilities exposed in incidents like the Change Healthcare breach.

A key leading indicator for sustainable growth is the number of customers generating over $100K in ARR. In Q2, we ended the quarter with 528 customers exceeding $100K ARR, marking a robust 17% sequential increase from 451 at the end of Q1 and a stellar 32% year-over-year growth from 400 in Q2 FY23. This represents approximately 12% of our total customer base of over 4,400, but these accounts drive roughly 65% of our total ARR, underscoring our land-and-expand model in action. Dollar-based net retention for this group remains elite at 128%—that's customers expanding their spend with us by an average of 28% annually through multi-product adoption and seat expansion.

We've seen accelerated adoption of our AI-powered Extended Detection and Response (XDR) platform, particularly integrations with leading SIEMs like Splunk Enterprise Security and Elastic Security, as well as EDR endpoints from partners like CrowdStrike Falcon and Microsoft Defender. In Q2, 72% of new $100K+ wins—that's 38 out of 53—included our GenAI Threat Hunter module, which leverages large language models for autonomous behavioral analytics and reduced mean-time-to-respond (MTTR) to under 5 minutes in live deployments. This is resonating amid the surge in AI-driven attacks, like the sophisticated phishing campaigns mimicking ChatGPT we've neutralized for clients.

Regionally, North America continues to dominate, accounting for 68% of this cohort with 359 customers, up 14% QoQ, fueled by U.S. federal mandates under CISA's Zero Trust Maturity Model and the Biden administration's cybersecurity executive orders. We're particularly pleased with EMEA growth, adding 42 new $100K+ logos to reach 112 total—a 49% YoY jump—driven by compliance with NIS2 Directive and DORA regulations, where our Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform (CNAPP) has become table stakes for banks and telcos. APAC is our fastest-growing frontier at 27% YoY to 51 customers, with strong traction in Japan and Australia amid rising state-sponsored threats from North Korea's Lazarus Group and China's Volt Typhoon actors targeting critical infrastructure.

Strategically, this isn't just about headcount; it's about sticky, high-LTV relationships. Our convergence strategy—bundling Secure Access Service Edge (SASE) with our Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) and Data Loss Prevention (DLP)—has driven a 40% upsell rate within this cohort, mirroring successes at peers like Zscaler and Palo Alto Networks. Post the MOVEit breach fallout and ongoing Log4j-style vulnerabilities, enterprises are consolidating vendors: 65% of expansions involved displacing legacy point solutions from Check Point or Symantec. We've also deepened hyperscaler partnerships, with AWS Marketplace and Azure Marketplace deals contributing 22% of Q2 $100K+ bookings.

Turning to billings performance, which came in ahead of our guidance range and reflects the strong demand environment. For the quarter, we delivered billings of $278 million, representing the high end of our updated outlook and a 28% year-over-year increase. This compares favorably to our initial Q2 guidance of $250 million to $260 million, which we had reaffirmed post our Q1 results amid ongoing macroeconomic pressures.

Billings capture the total value of subscriptions and professional services billed during the period, including deferred revenue uplift from multi-year contracts, serving as a leading indicator of our future revenue trajectory. This beat was driven by accelerated large deal closes, robust net retention, and early momentum from our GenAI SecureShield platform launch. We saw $85 million in ACV from new logos, up 35% year-over-year, fueled by wins in the hyperscaler ecosystem. Key deals included a $12 million multi-year contract with a top-5 cloud provider for our Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP), integrating seamlessly with their native Kubernetes services—think AWS EKS and Azure AKS. Upsell and cross-sell contributed $112 million in ACV, or 40% of total billings, with our dollar-based net retention rate holding steady at 118%—in line with peers like CrowdStrike's recent quarters.

Segment-wise, our core Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) business, powered by our ZetaXDR engine, generated $145 million in billings, beating our internal model by 8%. This was propelled by heightened ransomware activity—we're tracking a 42% YoY increase in LockBit and BlackCat variants per our threat intelligence feeds—driving urgency for our AI-native behavioral analytics. Cloud Security, now 32% of billings at $89 million, grew 52% YoY, outpacing the segment's overall market growth as forecasted by Gartner. Professional services billings hit $44 million, up 22%, tied to implementation of our Identity Threat Detection and Response (ITDR) module.

Regionally, the Americas remained our powerhouse at 62% of billings, or $172 million, up 25% YoY, with strength in U.S. federal via our FedRAMP High authorization. EMEA contributed 24%, or $67 million, accelerating 38% YoY on DORA regulation tailwinds. APAC, at 14% or $39 million, grew 22%. Our current remaining performance obligations (cRPO) stood at $1.42 billion, up 36% YoY and 12% quarter-over-quarter, with 85% expected to convert to revenue within the next 12 months. This visibility gives us confidence in our full-year billings guide of $1.15 billion to $1.18 billion.

Finally, on R&D investment, a key strategic lever. In the fiscal year to date mirroring our full-year trajectory, we've invested at 19.2% of revenue, scaling from 17.8% last year. For Q2 specifically, we deployed approximately $55 million—19% of quarterly revenue—growing 28% year-over-year. This puts us in line with peers: CrowdStrike around 24%, Palo Alto at 19-20%. Key initiatives include AI and ML advancements at 45% of budget for Sentinel AI, reducing MTTD to under 90 minutes; Zero-Trust and Cloud Security at 25% with post-quantum cryptography; OT/IoT at 15%; and emerging tech with headcount to 2,800 engineers.

Regionally tailored: North America prioritizes AI-driven XDR; EMEA for NIS2 tools; APAC sovereignty solutions. This positions us for FY2024 R&D at 18-20% of revenue, funding federated learning and more. Looking forward, Q3 spend guidance is $29-31 million for marketing, prioritizing high-ROI digital and ABM; continued CAC compression to $135,000 and ROMI to 5.2x; ARR growth of 11-13% QoQ; $100K+ customers to 600 by year-end; billings full-year 27-30% growth.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for the question and answer session. First question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Thanks, and congrats on a strong quarter. Jordan, can you expand on how the marketing efficiencies are translating to pipeline visibility amid longer sales cycles?

Jordan Lee: Thanks, John. Absolutely, our marketing optimizations have directly bolstered pipeline, with ABM yielding 15x ROAS and SQL velocity up 25% in APAC. Even with cycles at 9 months, our $200M+ pipeline is 55% skewed to $100K+ deals, supported by 95% gross retention.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen: Great, thanks. Alex or Jordan, thoughts on competitive dynamics in cloud security post recent launches?

Alex Rivera: Lisa, our platformization is key—76% multi-product adoption, displacing point solutions. Customer feedback on Nexus CloudShield shows 84% seeing 50%+ misconfig improvements, positioning us strongly against Prisma and others.

Operator: Next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan.

Mike Rodriguez: Thanks. Taylor, how is R&D fueling AI innovations against gen-AI threats?

Taylor Kim: Mike, our 19% R&D intensity funds Sentinel AI, with multimodal LLMs preempting polymorphic malware. Beta tests show 40% faster MTTR, and we're integrating federated learning for multi-cloud, outpacing evasion rates in MITRE evals.

Operator: Next question comes from Emily Patel with Barclays.

Emily Patel: Hi, team. Morgan, any updates on threat landscape adaptations for customers?

Morgan Patel: Emily, we're constantly monitoring, with Nexus AI Sentinel live in 4,200 accounts neutralizing LockBit variants and AI phishing. Our telemetry from 15B events drives proactive updates, aligning with NIS2 and CMMC for customer resilience.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We believe we are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for cybersecurity solutions. Thank you to our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
